'''Bennett Stirtz''' (born October 3, 2003) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Northwest Missouri State Bearcats men's basketball|Northwest Missouri State Bearcats]], [[Drake Bulldogs men's basketball|Drake Bulldogs]] and [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa Hawkeyes]].

==Early life and high school==
Stirtz grew up in [[Liberty, Missouri]] and attended [[Liberty High School (Liberty, Missouri)|Liberty High School]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/drake/drake-bulldogs/2024/12/11/bennett-stirtz-drake-basketball-vs-kansas-state-game-preview-bulldogs-wildcats-k-state/76829793007/|title=Bennett Stirtz, a lifelong Kansas State fan, all about Drake basketball in upcoming game|work=[[The Des Moines Register]]|date=December 11, 2024|access-date=March 4, 2025}}</ref> He played basketball at Liberty and was coached by his father.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kshb.com/sports/local-sports/high-school/dynamic-father-son-duo-lead-liberty-blue-jays-to-victory|title=Dynamic father-son duo lead Liberty Blue Jays to victory|first=McKenzie|last=Nelson|website=KSHB.com|date=January 5, 2022|access-date=March 4, 2025}}</ref> Stirtz was named first-team All-State as a senior after averaging 18.3 points, 6.8 rebounds, 4 assists, and 2.5 steals per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/high-school/article259400499.html|title=Kansas City's DiRenna Awards finalists high school hoops|work=[[The Kansas City Star]]|date=March 14, 2022|access-date=March 4, 2025}}</ref>

==College career==
Stirtz began his college career at [[Northwest Missouri State Bearcats men's basketball|Northwest Missouri State]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6028371/2025/01/02/drake-bulldogs-basketball-ben-mccollum-transfers/|title=Can a team led by Division II transfers become college hoops' most dangerous mid-major?|first=CJ|last=Moore|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=January 2, 2025|access-date=March 4, 2025}}</ref> He was named the [[Mid-America Intercollegiate Athletics Association]] (MIAA) Freshman of the Year and second-team All-MIAA in his first season with the Bearcats.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://fox4kc.com/sports/college/nw-missouri-state/liberty-alum-bennett-stirtz-leads-nw-missouri-state-to-miaa-tournament-title/|title=Liberty alum Bennett Stirtz leads NW Missouri State to MIAA tournament title|first=PJ|last=Green|website=FOX4KC.com|date=March 6, 2023|access-date=March 4, 2025}}</ref> Stirtz repeated as a second-team All-MIAA selection as a sophomore after averaging 15.2 points, 3.5 rebounds, 3.5 assists, and 1.4 steals per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kq2.com/news/northwest-missouri-state-guard-bennett-stirtz-transferring-to-drake/article_428f17c6-fc36-11ee-ab3d-b31c5000e09e.html|title=Northwest Missouri State's Bennett Stirtz, Isaiah Jackson and Daniel Abreu transferring to Drake|first=Brett|last=Kennedy|website=KQ2.com|date=April 16, 2024|access-date=March 4, 2025}}</ref>

Stirtz transferred to [[Drake Bulldogs men's basketball|Drake]] after his sophomore season, following former Northwest Missouri head coach [[Ben McCollum]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/drake/drake-bulldogs/2024/04/16/drake-bulldogs-basketball-commitment-bennett-stirtz-ben-mccollum/73342487007/|title=Three Northwest Missouri State basketball players follow Ben McCollum to Drake|work=[[The Des Moines Register]]|date=April 16, 2024|access-date=January 30, 2025}}</ref> He was named the [[Missouri Valley Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year]] and the conference Newcomer of the Year at the end of the regular season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/drake/drake-bulldogs/2025/03/06/drake-basketball-ben-mccollum-arch-madness-ncaa-tournament-bennett-stirtz/81151380007/|title=Drake's Bennett Stirtz wins Missouri Valley Player of the Year, Ben McCollum wins Coach of Year|work=[[The Des Moines Register]]|date=March 6, 2025|access-date=March 7, 2025}}</ref>

After one season at Drake, Stirtz announced he would be entering the transfer portal and following McCollum to the University of Iowa.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hawkcentral.com/story/sports/college/iowa/basketball-men/2025/03/25/iowa-basketball-bennett-stirtz-drake-transfer-nba-draft-hawkeyes-ben-mccollum-hawkeyes/82653046007/|title=Drake's Bennett Stirtz on decision to transfer to Iowa basketball: 'Glad to be a Hawkeye'|work=The Des Moines Register|date=March 25, 2025|access-date=March 25, 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Stirtz is the son of Roger and Renee Stirtz. He has three siblings: Mason, Caden and Cooper.<ref>{{cite web |title=BENNETT STIRTZ |url=https://hawkeyesports.com/sports/mbball/roster/player/bennett-stirtz |website=hawkeyesports.com |access-date=26 March 2026}}</ref>

Stirtz is a [[Christianity|Christian]]. He has said, “Win or lose, give glory to God. He gave me a platform and I just want to use it for Him.“<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ackerman |first1=Jon |title=Bennett Stirtz leads Iowa into Sweet 16 for first time since 1999: ‘Win or lose, give glory to God’ |url=https://sportsspectrum.com/sport/basketball/2026/03/23/bennett-stirtz-iowa-sweet-16-win-lose-glory-god/ |website=Sports Spectrum |access-date=26 March 2026}}</ref>
